question.text: The Byzantine capital was this city, which was renamed Istanbul after it fell to the Ottomans.
question.clue: A bronze column originally from Delphi which depicted three entwined serpents holding up a golden bowl was relocated to this city's Hippodrome.

swap.text: Theodora may have influenced her husband to include women's rights in this legal code that is contained within the Corpus Juris Civilis . This legal code was created to specify the laws of the Byzantine Empire under its namesake emperor.
swap.clue: This work contains strikingly accurate transcription of quotes by Gaius and includes several writings by Ulpian as part of the Pandects, or Digest.

question.leadin: His campaigns against the Vandals and the Ostrogoths were much aided by his generals Narses and Belisarius.
question.text: Identify this ruler who built the Hagia Sophia and recodified laws in Corpus Juris Civilis.
question.answerHtml: Justinian I or Justinian the Great [prompt on partial answer]
question.answer: Justinian I or Justinian the Great
question.clue: Much of the history of this leader was recorded by Procopius , who traveled with his general Belisarius .

swap.leadin: This man employed the mathematicians Anthemius and Isidoros to construct the building with which he is associated.
swap.text: Name this Byzantine emperor whose reign saw the establishment of a new law code and the construction of the Hagia Sophia.
swap.answerHtml: Justinian I [or Justinian the Great; or Flavius Justinianus; or Petrus Sabbatius; prompt on “Justinian”]
swap.clue: This ruler, who was the subject of The Secret History by Procopius, has his generals Mundus and Belisarius put down a revolt by the Blues and the Greens.

question.leadin: This leader commissioned Isidore of Miletus to build the Hagia Sophia.
question.text: Name this Byzantine Emperor of the 6th century C.E known as "the Great".
question.clue: After rival chariot factions who separated into the Blues and the Greens rioted in this ruler's capital city, he chose Isidore of Miletus and Anthemius of Tralles to rebuild a structure that would eventually be turned into a mosque in 1453.

swap.leadin: This woman apocryphally declared that "purple is the noblest shroud" during the Nika Riots.
swap.text: Name this empress of the Byzantine Empire who met her husband Justinian through their shared support for the Blue faction of the demes.
swap.clue: A ruler with this name, who as a child acted in a portrayal of Leda and the Swan, was called the "most depraved" in the Anecdota.

question.leadin: Description acceptable. Isidore of Kiev apocryphally survived this event by dressing up a dead body with his clothes so that it would be beheaded instead of him.
question.text: Name this event for which the engineer Orban designed a cannon known as "The Basilic" to destroy the Theodosian Walls.
question.answerHtml: Fall of Constantinople [accept answers generally describing a Siege of Constantinople; accept BUT DO NOT REVEAL answers indicating that Constantinople being is captured by the Ottomans; accept the end of the Byzantine Empire]
question.clue: Giovanni Giustiniani ordered his ships to defend the Golden Horn during this event, which also saw which saw one side utilize Orban's "Basilica" cannons.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Byzantine Empire.
swap.text: This Byzantine emperor lost the Battle of the Gates of Trajan to Tsar Samuel. However, this ruler got his revenge at the Battle of Kleidion where he gained his most notorious nickname after blinding prisoners.
swap.answerHtml: Basil II [accept Basil the Bulgar Slayer or Basil Porphyrogenitus; Prompt on “Basil”]
swap.clue: John Geometres wrote of how the "arrows of the Moesians broke the spears of the Avzonians" in describing this ruler's loss at the Battle of the Gates of Trajan.

question.leadin: Identify the following about some military units charged with protecting heads of state.
question.text: Known for bearing axes and being comprised largely of Scandinavians, these troops were the guards of the Byzantine Empire. This unit was established by Basil II.
question.clue: As punishment for replacing this group with loyal Scythians, Michael V ("the fifth") was castrated and blinded by Harald Hardrada.

swap.leadin: Fulk of Neuilly agitated for this event.
swap.text: Name this campaign whose disastrous result occurred after a meeting with Philip of Swabia, the taking of Zara at the behest of Enrico Dandolo, and an attempt to overthrow Alexius III.
swap.clue: In order to obtain the support of one city state, the participants of this event agreed to sack the city of Zara in Hungary.

question.leadin: Answer the following questions about the Great Schism of 1054.
question.text: One of the major ideological differences between the two halves of the Church was the addition of this clause to the Nicene Creed. It states that the spirit proceeds from the "father and son" rather than just the "father".
question.clue: This clause that was added to the Nicene Creed in 589 at the Council of Toledo. Its Latin name means "and the son," and it implies that the Holy Spirit proceeds from both God the father and his Son, Jesus. .

swap.leadin: The Assyrian monk Alopen was a follower of this leader and brought his ideas to the Tang dynasty as the first known Christian missionary to China.
swap.text: Name this fourth century Archbishop of Constantinople who taught that Christ had two distinct natures, human and divine. During the second half of the fifth century, a church named for this man flourished in Syria.
swap.clue: This Patriarch was deposed by the Council of Ephesus for his refusal to call Mary the "Mother of God," and his views that Christ had two persons. His ideas were subsequently embraced by the Assyrian Church of the East.

question.leadin: The "Headless Council" at Hieria, so nicknamed because none of the five great patriarchs were there, was convened by Constantine V to support this policy.
question.text: Name this Byzantine policy which opposed the veneration of religious images.
question.clue: The first attempt to apply this doctrine officially was met with resistance at the Chalke Gate, and it was condemned by the Second Council of Nicaea convoked by Irene.

swap.text: The Council of Clermont was ostensibly called to assist this embattled Byzantine emperor, who did not ask for a full-scale invasion of the Holy Land. Still, he took advantage of the Crusade to regain lost territory in Anatolia.
swap.clue: The insane monk Raiktor joined a force against this man that won the Battle of Dyrrhachium and Robert Guiscard.

question.text: After the Battle of Adrianople, the Bulgar tsar Kaloyan made a cup from the skull of the first Latin Emperor, who had this name. The final ruler of the Latin Empire, who sold the Crown of Thorns to Louis IX, also had this name.
question.answerHtml: Baldwin [or Baudouin; or Baldwin I; or Baldwin II; or Baldwin of Courtenay]
question.clue: This cousin of Rudyard Kipling highlighted the power of aerial attacks by noting that "the bomber will always get through."

swap.leadin: The Arsenites and Josephists feuded over support for this ruler, whom Patriarch Arsenios Autoreianos had excommunicated in 1261 for ordering the blinding of the eleven-year-old John IV Laskaris.
swap.text: Name this ruler whose policies were juxtaposed with those of his son, Andronikos II, by the contemporaneous historian George Pachymeres ("pack-ih-MEER-eez").
swap.clue: This figure's diplomatic acumen and willingness to bankrupt his treasury helped Pedro III of Aragon, overthrowing Charles of Anjou in the Sicilian Vespers.

question.leadin: The Arvanites under Peter Bua rose up in revolt in this principality in the 15th century.
question.text: Name this principality in the Peloponnese that was first ruled over by Manuel Kantakouzenos in 1349. Along with Epirus, the despot of this region was usually a son of the Byzantine Emperor.

swap.text: The second ruler of this dynasty, Leo VI the Wise, prescribed harsh punishments for counterfeiting alchemists in his Book of the Eparch. Leo completed the Basilika law code named after the founder of this dynasty, Basil I.
swap.clue: Chief military figures from this period include Nicephorus Phocas and an Armenian usurper, John Tzimisces, though its most notable battlefield accomplishment may have come against the army of Tsar Samuel.

question.leadin: In one work, this author describes the Norman woman Sikelgaita as "like another Pallas, if not a second Athena," in a text that also includes an account of the Battle of Dyrrhachium.
question.text: Name this historian, who was exiled to a monastery after a failed coup attempt against John II.
question.clue: This woman may have been inspired by the material laid out by her husband Nikephoros Bryennios the Younger to write a chronicle of her father's rule named the Alexiad.

swap.text: This archbishop of Thessalonica is known for his eyewitness account of the city's sack by and the Odyssey . Norman forces in 1185 and for a set of commentaries on the Iliad
